short: ASR-teacher labels (M02) were new to lip reading (0 of 77 earlier) but standard: the distillation term is untested in WER and the no-label LRS2 gain is 0.3 points, one run.
position: The paper [@afouras2020asr] changes the training labels (M02): an audio-only ASR teacher supplies transcripts and posteriors for unlabelled video. This departed from lip-reading practice, where none of the 77 earlier studies used ASR-generated labels, distillation or unlabelled video (pattern match, Appendix). The verdict is standard: the authors name cross-modal ASR distillation for audio-visual recognition as the closest work (§1.1), and no Table 3 row trains CTC on ASR transcripts without distillation, so the distillation term is untested in WER. The "no human labels" LRS2 result is a 0.3-point single-run difference, below V2P's 0.9-point bootstrap error on LRS3 [@shillingford2018] (inference); the 3.9-point LRS3 gain from an ASR-filtered VoxCeleb2 subset is the better-supported finding (inference). The public-data state-of-the-art claim (M12) rests on 0.3- and 0.4-point margins over the [concurrent] Conv-seq2seq (inference).
